title: Reduced cell-based PIN1 polar auxin transport model on the epidermal (L1) mesh of the curd dome — parameters, geometry and literature anchors

model_sources.citation: Jönsson H, Heisler MG, Shapiro BE, Meyerowitz EM, Mjolsness E (2006) PNAS 103(5):1633-1638
model_sources.role: Up-the-gradient PIN1 allocation P_ij = P_tot * A_j / (kappa + sum_k A_k) and the auxin balance dA_i/dt = c - d A_i + D sum_j (A_j - A_i) + T sum_j (P_ji A_j - P_ij A_i) on a cellular template of the shoot apex; emergent spiral phyllotaxis with divergence near 137.5 deg

model_sources.citation: Smith RS, Guyomarc'h S, Mandel T, Reinhardt D, Kuhlemeier C, Prusinkiewicz P (2006) PNAS 103(5):1301-1306
model_sources.role: Primordia as auxin sinks on a growing apex; threshold-triggered initiation in the peripheral zone; cells advected outward by growth and produced in the central zone

model_sources.citation: Reinhardt D, Pesce E-R, Stieger P, Mandel T, Baltensperger K, Bennett M, Traas J, Friml J, Kuhlemeier C (2003) Nature 426:255-260
model_sources.role: PIN1-dependent polar auxin transport is required for primordium initiation: pin1 mutants and NPA-treated apices form naked pin inflorescences (the T = 0 ablation reference, expected initiation ratio 0)

model_sources.citation: Douady S, Couder Y (1992) Physical Review Letters 68(13):2098-2101
model_sources.role: Hofmeister-rule inhibitory-field dynamics: new primordia appear in the largest free gap of the initiation ring; initiation rate scales with the ring perimeter, r_p(R) = k R

model_sources.citation: Smyth DR, Bowman JL, Meyerowitz EM (1990) The Plant Cell 2(8):755-767
model_sources.role: Golden divergence angle 137.5 deg of spiral phyllotaxis in Arabidopsis (reference for the emergent divergence angle)

geometries.note: Both the hemispherical Cauliflower dome and the Romanesco cone are represented as cones of the matching H/R; cone half-angle alpha = atan(R/H). Cells are uniformly distributed over the cone surface so that the cell count scales with pi * R * sqrt(R^2 + H^2).

model_parameters.note: Dimensionless; chosen so that the inhibitory (sink) diameter is ~3-4 times smaller than the initiation-ring circumference at R = 1 (the regime in which Douady-Couder / Smith et al. models produce spiral phyllotaxis). They are not fitted to any Brassica measurement.

coupling_to_plastochron_law.statement: r_p(R) = k R (perimeter scaling) with meristem growth R(tau) = R0 + v_r tau gives r_p(tau)/r_p(R0) = 1 + (k / r_p(R0)) v_r tau, i.e. Law-2 beta = (k / r_p(R0)) * v_r
coupling_to_plastochron_law.v_r_source: radial_expansion_rate_v_r = 0.16 in roman_esco_fractal_inflorescence_reference.json (Pass 1 vendored value, not traced to a specific figure of Azpeitia et al. 2021)

limitations: Not a continuum finite-element solve of PIN1 transport on the curved manifold; cells are discrete points with k-NN (k = 6) adjacency rebuilt every 20 steps as they are advected.
The hemispherical dome is approximated by a cone of equal H/R.
Sink fields are isotropic Gaussians in 3D Euclidean distance, not geodesic distance on the surface.
Emergent divergence angles scatter (MAD ~ 10-25 deg) because of the jittered mesh and discrete threshold initiation; the model is not tuned for angular precision.
